To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
802.11 MAC layer has a positive impact on both AODV and CSMA routing protocols in MANETs and 802.11 has a negative impact on LAR in MANETS.
AODV and 802.11 MAC layer are suitable for low density networks whereas CSMA MAC layer is not suitable for MANETs with low density.
the MAC protocol has significant impact on the performance of the routing protocols in MANETS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance of two on demand routing algorithms AODV and DSR in MANETs using two different MAC protocols.
the performance evaluation of AODV and DSR routing protocols under different MAC layer protocols.
the effect of MAC layer on AODV, LAR routing protocols in MANETs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
802.11 MAC protocol is better than CSMA in terms of performance in AODV and CSMA in LAR routing protocols.
the performance of both routing protocols AODVs and LAR is better with 802.11 than CSMA.
802.11 has a better performance than CSMA for AODV and CSMA has better performance than 802.11 for LAR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AODV is suitable for CSMA MAC protocol while LAR is suitable for 802.11 MAC protocol.
802.11 MAC layer is suitable for both AODV and DSR routing protocols.
AODV is more suitable for MANETs where as LAR is not suitable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MAC layer has significant impact on the performance of the routing protocols.
the MAC protocol used has an impact on routing protocols in MANETs and hence should be taken into consideration when selecting routing protocols for MANETs.
the performance of AODV is better than LAR in MANETS.
